newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks hit new record on dollar, rate hopes.
newsitem.headline: French stocks hit new record on dollar, rate hopes.

text.p: French stocks rallied on Wednesday to a record close on the dollar's strength and expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will not raise U.S. interest rates, brokers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 38.18 points, or 1.53 percent, at 2,541.25, surpassing the previous closing record set last Friday of 2,516.56 points.
The index hit an all-time intraday high of 2,544.06 points.
The CAC-40 February futures contract rose 37 points to settle at 2,546.
Volume was a heavy 9.4 billion francs, including 6.8 billion on the CAC-40.

Traders said the financial markets expected the Fed to let rates alone after a two-day Federal Open Markets Committee meeting ending later on Wednesday. The bourse was also helped by bond prices, which were bolstered by a drop in German industry orders in December.

Traders see resistance on the CAC-40 at between 2,549-57 points and again at 2,563 points. They also expect investors to turn cautious ahead of the market-moving U.S. unemployment figures for January due out on Friday.
"The bourse is very well oriented despite the FOMC meeting today. Everyone is anticipating a monetary status quo," a trader said.
But some market operators were feeling less sanguine.

"I recommend extreme prudence because I think the market's oversold," said Olivier Blitz at brokerage IFF. "The market's counting on the Fed not to raise interest rates but I think that if the Fed does nothing, that could be dangerous."
The market has gained nearly 10 percent since the beginning of the year after ending 1996 23.71 percent higher to catch up with the bull markets in Europe and the United States.
Much of the activity centred on shares in companies that released sales results or in those involved in restructurings.
Skin care and cosmetics company Clarins rallied as high as 809 francs after reporting a 15.8 percent rise in 1996 sales and forecasting double-digit profit growth for the year.
But market rumours of a convertible bond issue dragged the share back from its highs.
